newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money firms to 3.05/10 pct on demand.
newsitem.headline: German call money firms to 3.05/10 pct on demand.

text.p: German call money rates on Monday were slightly higher at 3.05/10 percent from Friday's level of 2.975/3.05 percent after the Bundesbank set the September minimum reserve level at 37.7 billion marks.
"The market is a bit stretched right now" after the reserve levels were announced, one trader said.
Call money rates were largely expected to stay at current levels during the near-term amid healthy demand for funds by banks to meeting month-end reserve requirements.
But some traders said rates were likely to slide toward 3.00 percent, the fixed-rate repo level, during the session.
Commercial bank reserves at the Bundesbank as of Friday were seen at 36.8 billion marks, down from 37.1 billion marks on Thursday.
The monthly average as of Sunday fell to 38.3 billion marks from 38.6 billion marks from Friday, while Lombard borrowings totaled about 100 million marks.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average FIONA= on Monday was pegged at 3.09100 compared with 3.05100 on Friday.
